document.lead: You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.

text: Some of the world’s most famous museums display sculptures, manuscripts and jewellery that were removed from their places of origin centuries ago. I largely agree that such objects should be returned when they were taken by force or under unequal conditions, although careful arrangements are needed to ensure that they remain protected and accessible.

The main argument for return is one of justice. Many treasures were acquired through looting, military conquest or agreements that local people had no real power to refuse, and keeping them today means continuing to benefit from that injustice. Moreover, these objects often carry deep cultural or religious meaning for the communities that created them, whereas in a foreign museum they may be just one exhibit among thousands, seen by visitors who know little of its original purpose.

Returning artefacts can also benefit the countries that receive them. A famous object displayed in its homeland can attract visitors, support local museums and help younger generations connect with their heritage. In recent years, several European museums have returned items such as the Benin Bronzes to Nigeria, showing that restitution is practical as well as fair.

Admittedly, opponents raise legitimate concerns. Some countries of origin may lack the facilities to preserve fragile items, and large international museums allow millions of people to see treasures from many cultures in one place. However, these problems can be solved through cooperation, for example by training conservators, sharing exhibitions and arranging long-term loans.
In conclusion, objects taken by force should, in principle, go back to the peoples they belong to. With international cooperation, their return need not reduce the public’s access to world heritage.

note.en: A condition within the position: protection and access.
note.kk: Ұстанымның ішіндегі шарт: сақталуы және қолжетімділігі.
note.ru: Условие внутри позиции: сохранность и доступ.

note.en: The topic sentence of the main argument.
Adds a second point about the objects’ meaning.
note.kk: Заттардың маңызы туралы екінші дәлелді қосады.
note.ru: Добавляет второй довод о смысле предметов.

note.en: Contrasts the object’s homeland with a foreign museum.
note.kk: Заттың отанын бөгде мұражайға қарсы қояды.
note.ru: Противопоставляет родину предмета и чужой музей.

note.en: Adds a point about the benefit to the country.
note.ru: Добавляет довод о пользе для страны.

note.en: Shows that return is both fair and practical.
note.kk: Қайтарудың әрі әділ, әрі жүзеге асатынын көрсетеді.
note.ru: Показывает, что возврат и справедлив, и осуществим.

note.en: Turns to the reply to the concession.

strengths.en: The writer agrees for objects taken by force — more precise than “return everything”.
strengths.kk: Автор күшпен алынған заттарға қатысты келіседі — бұл «бәрін қайтару» дегеннен дәлірек.
strengths.ru: Автор согласен для предметов, взятых силой, — это точнее, чем «вернуть всё».
strengths.example: when they were taken by force or under unequal conditions

strengths.en: The Benin Bronzes show that restitution is already happening.
strengths.kk: Бенин қолалары қайтарудың іс жүзінде болып жатқанын дәлелдейді.
strengths.ru: Бенинские бронзы доказывают, что возврат уже происходит на практике.
strengths.example: several European museums have returned items such as the Benin Bronzes to Nigeria

strengths.en: Both opposing points are accepted and given a practical answer.
strengths.kk: Қарсыластардың екі дәлелі де мойындалып, практикалық жауап алады.
strengths.ru: Оба довода противников признаны и получают практичный ответ.
strengths.example: by training conservators, sharing exhibitions and arranging long-term loans

strengths.en: Topic vocabulary: looting, restitution, conservators, heritage — Lexical Resource 8.
strengths.kk: Тақырып сөздері: looting, restitution, conservators, heritage — Lexical Resource 8.
strengths.ru: Слова темы: looting, restitution, conservators, heritage — Lexical Resource 8.
strengths.example: Many treasures were acquired through looting, military conquest

note.en: Introduction: a familiar museum scene and a “largely agree” position with a condition.
note.kk: Кіріспе: мұражай залдарының таныс көрінісі және шарты бар «негізінен келісемін» ұстанымы.
note.ru: Введение: знакомая картина музейных залов и позиция «в основном согласен» с условием.

note.en: The main argument — justice, and the meaning of the object for the people who made it.
note.kk: Басты дәлел — әділдік және заттың оны жасаған халық үшін маңызы.
note.ru: Главный довод — справедливость и смысл предмета для народа, который его создал.

note.en: The second argument — the benefit to the country of origin; a real example — the Benin Bronzes.
note.kk: Екінші дәлел — шыққан елге пайдасы; нақты мысал — Бенин қолаларының қайтарылуы.
note.ru: Второй довод — польза для страны происхождения; реальный пример — Бенинские бронзы.

note.en: Concession and reply: preservation and access can be solved through cooperation.
note.kk: Мойындау және жауап: сақталуы мен қолжетімділігі — ынтымақтастық арқылы шешіледі.
note.ru: Уступка и ответ: сохранность и доступ — решаются сотрудничеством.

note.en: Conclusion: the principle and the condition for carrying it out.
note.kk: Қорытынды: қағида және оны орындаудың шарты.
note.ru: Вывод: принцип и условие его выполнения.

document.title: Returning cultural treasures
document.question:
Many museums hold historical objects that were taken from other countries, often during periods of war or colonial rule. Some people believe that these objects should be returned to their countries of origin.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
